$schema_note: Points where SI 2017/752 does not determine an outcome, found by reading the retrieved XML clause by clause. None resolved.
note: P6 is the counterpart of the Banxico Dias question in position but not in kind. There the ambiguity was the UNIT of a period. Here the period is unambiguous, 13 months from the debit date, and the open question is whether a second, qualitative limb bars the remedy independently of it. A source can be structurally precise and still leave the operative question open.

ambiguities.question: The fraud carve-out disapplies paragraph (2) only. Does the refund obligation in paragraph (1) survive with no deadline, or is it suspended?

readings.basis: The text disapplies `paragraph (2)` by number and says nothing about paragraph (1). Paragraph (1) is a freestanding `must refund`.

readings.reading: Obligation is suspended while grounds subsist
readings.basis: Refunding immediately while notifying under the tipping-off provisions would defeat the purpose of the carve-out, which exists so a provider is not forced to act on a transaction it suspects.

ambiguities.textual_basis: reg 76(3): `Paragraph (2) does not apply where...`. reg 76(1): `the payment service provider must refund`.
ambiguities.materiality: Decisive on every suspected-fraud case. One reading leaves a live obligation with no time limit; the other leaves no obligation at all until grounds fall away.

ambiguities.question: When does a provider `become aware` of an unauthorised transaction, and whose awareness counts?

readings.reading: On receipt of the user's notification under reg 74
readings.basis: The two provisions are part of one process and the notification is the event the regulations create.
The text says `becomes aware`, not `is notified`, and reg 74 uses the notification language explicitly where it means it. A provider's own fraud monitoring could trigger it first.

ambiguities.textual_basis: reg 76(2) `the day on which it becomes aware`, against reg 74(1) `notifies the payment service provider`. Different words in adjacent provisions of the same process.
ambiguities.materiality: Sets the clock start for the only hard deadline in the refund obligation.

ambiguities.question: Where the provider failed to supply Part 6 information, is the whole of reg 74(1) disapplied, or only the 13 month limb?

readings.basis: 74(2) says the user is entitled to redress `notwithstanding that the payment service user has failed to notify... as mentioned in that paragraph`, and that paragraph contains both limbs.
The mischief is the user not knowing about the transaction because information was withheld. `Without undue delay` runs from awareness, so it is unaffected by the information failure.

ambiguities.textual_basis: reg 74(1) carries two limbs in one sentence; reg 74(2) refers back to `that paragraph` without distinguishing them.
ambiguities.materiality: Determines whether a user who knew and sat on it for two years is still barred where information was also withheld.

ambiguities.question: What makes restoration of the account `applicable`?

readings.reading: Whenever the debit produced knock-on effects
readings.basis: Interest, charges and returned items are the mischief; restoring the state means undoing those too.

readings.reading: Only where the refund alone leaves the account in a different state
readings.basis: Reads `where applicable` as a narrow saver for cases the refund does not already cure.

ambiguities.textual_basis: reg 76(1)(b) `where applicable, restore the debited payment account to the state it would have been in`.
ambiguities.materiality: Sets the boundary of the remedy beyond the principal amount.

ambiguities.question: `not in itself necessarily sufficient` leaves open what would be sufficient. What must accompany instrument use to discharge the burden?

readings.reading: A matter for the tribunal on the whole evidence
readings.basis: `necessarily` signals that the question is fact-specific rather than rule-determined.
75(1) enumerates what must be proved; 75(3) then denies that instrument use alone proves them.

ambiguities.materiality: Determines whether the burden can ever be discharged from records alone.

ambiguities.question: Does failing to notify `without undue delay`, while still inside 13 months, bar redress on its own?

readings.basis: The sentence reads `only if it notifies... without undue delay, and in any event no later than 13 months`. Both are stated as requirements of the same entitlement.

readings.reading: No, the 13 months is the operative bar
readings.basis: `and in any event` reads as a longstop qualifying the first limb rather than adding an independent bar.

ambiguities.textual_basis: reg 74(1), a single sentence carrying both limbs joined by `and in any event`.
ambiguities.materiality: Decides whether a judgment clause sits on the path to losing the remedy, or whether the remedy turns only on a date.
